title: Starting a kingdom
summary: The exact new-game state and first production chain.

sections.title: Starting state
paragraphs: A new player receives mine and forge technologies, the iron_ingot recipe, and mine_iron_ore through the mine callback. Iron-ore resource capacity starts at 1. The only placed machine is a Forge configured for iron ingots at world position (-128,64), with five iron-ore items buffered in its first input. There is one workflow and no initial currency grant in CreateNewPlayer.

Shop is a free technology after Forge, but is not explicitly pre-purchased by CreateNewPlayer. Blacksmith grants iron_armor; Supply Depot additionally requires Mine automation and grants the wood-plank supply technology. Technology grants do not place machines.

sections.title: New Game and Continue
paragraphs: The main menu clears the in-memory player. New Game calls Bootstrap.InitNewGame; Continue loads the newest save by filesystem last-write time. GameManager tries the latest save if no in-memory player exists and creates a new player only if no latest save exists. A corrupt newest save can raise a load error; LoadLatestSave does not search older files automatically.

sections.title: Every workflow runs
paragraphs: WorldFlowManager starts and updates GamePlayer with Unity Time.deltaTime. Player resource quota recalculates on roughly 0.1-second ticks, war progress on roughly 2-second ticks, and GameTime counts simulated seconds. Every workflow is updated, including workflows not currently selected.

title: Technology requirements and unlocking
summary: Parents, prerequisite lists, special gates, hidden content, and purchases.

sections.title: Requirements combine
paragraphs: A node is locked when Root is unpurchased, Previous is unpurchased, any AdditionalRequirements entry is unpurchased, or CustomRequirement returns false. Root organizes the branch and also gates it; Previous expresses another purchase prerequisite. Available means unpurchased, unlocked, and not Hidden for this player.

HasWarStage(type,stage) checks current war stage index ≥ stage. Since completed stages advance the index, a requirement stated as stage 1 means finishing the first stage, not merely having the war unlocked.

sections.title: Branch tier versus cost tier
paragraphs: The eleven tier articles group declarations by their T1–T11 source-class prefix. An early branch can contain late-game recipes with higher explicit cost tiers. An unspecified cost tier inherits from Previous, otherwise Root. A missing Root inherits Previous.Root when available. Default currency is set from the resulting cost tier.

Tier tables list every explicit new TechNode declaration. Shared automation helpers add further nodes, explained in Automation technology. Declared cost overrides take precedence over defaults. Resolved entity data and the in-game tooltip give the final price.

sections.title: Purchases and grants
paragraphs: A left click on an available node spends its full currency collection, marks it unlocked, invokes OnUnlock, updates the tree, and refreshes the tooltip. Free technologies can still need a click unless an unlock callback grants them. AddTech rejects DevMode nodes.

sections.title: Hidden and developer content
paragraphs: dev_item_spawner is DevMode. turtle_statue is always hidden. Several store-channel technologies are also always hidden, and graveyard_productivity is hidden after its default upgrade is created. Tier tables mark explicit hidden declarations. The all-tech achievement excludes hidden and developer nodes. Code presence alone does not prove normal availability.

title: Automation and shared machine upgrades
summary: Worker, extra slots, quality, and productivity research.

sections.title: Default family
paragraphs: AddDefaultUpgrades creates Worker, second slot, productivity, quality, and third slot technologies. Some branches use custom subsets or replace prices afterward. These researches allow upgrades or slots; they do not purchase and install the actual worker or upgrade on every machine.

rows: One slot and Worker upgrade available
Worker tech, war_effort, plus tier currency-system prerequisites

sections.title: Additional slot-two requirements
paragraphs: The helper starts with war_effort. Based on DEFAULT tier currency, it then adds requisition_office for Requisition, war_effort for Medals, quest_board for Rings, or dungeon for Ducats. Duplicated war_effort entries are possible. Later per-node currency overrides do not recalculate that list.

sections.title: Quality variants
paragraphs: Mine, resource suppliers, Forest, Farm, Barracks recruiting, and Training Grounds use specialized Artisan types. Normal crafting uses Artisan. Productivity wording depends on whether the machine processes equipment and enhancements. Individual machine branches can substitute specialized upgrades and slot rules. The tier articles preserve helper calls and post-creation overrides.

title: Technology cost formula
summary: Deterministic prices, type multipliers, currency conversion, rounding, and prestige.

sections.title: Raw price
paragraphs: At technology cost tier t, P = 400 × typeMultiplier × CostMultiplier × 2^(t−1) × R. R is a deterministic pseudorandom float in [0.92,1.10), seeded from the identifier. Prices do not reroll whenever a menu opens. A zero multiplier creates a free empty collection. Gold numbers in this formula are stored smallest-coin units: 100 units = 1 silver and 10,000 = 1 displayed gold coin.

sections.title: Each currency is a separate charge
paragraphs: Gold = RoundGold(truncate(P × GoldMultiplier × (1 if tier≤1 else 2))). Each non-gold charge is ceil(P/referenceGoldValue); Faith and Ingenuity are then halved with integer division. Gold plus Ducats means both charges, not a split total.
Normal RoundGold leaves values below 10,000 unchanged, rounds 10,000–999,999 to hundreds, and rounds 1,000,000 or more to ten-thousands. The helper supports another maxCount mode for other callers.

sections.title: Prestige and caching
paragraphs: TechCostReduce multiplies the generated collection by 1−perkValue and rounds each result with Math.Round. TechNode caches costs; GameManager resets every cached cost at scene start. Explicit currency/multiplier overrides take priority. Non-technology buildings share CreateCost but use a different tier-scaling branch.

title: Currencies and currency exchange
summary: All nine currencies and exact exchange rates and taxes.

headers: Reference value in raw Gold units

sections.title: Reference values
paragraphs: Values convert generated gold-equivalent costs into secondary currency amounts and provide exchange base rates. Balances and earned totals are separate. Spending a collection first checks affordability of every included currency.

sections.title: Exchange
paragraphs: currency_exchange follows Inventor; currency_exchange_tax follows it. Base tax is 1.0 (100%). Tax research halves it to 0.5. Prestige then multiplies tax by 1−CurrencyTaxReduce value.

Buying A units at reference value V costs truncate(A×V×(1+tax)) raw Gold units. Selling yields truncate(A×V/(1+tax)). At base tax, a Requisition costs 2,000 raw units (20 silver) and sells for 500 (5 silver); with only tax research it costs 1,500 (15 silver) and sells for 666 (6 silver, 66 copper).

sections.title: Income statistics
paragraphs: Exchange outputs use isIncome=false and do not count as earned Gold. Buy slider maximum uses affordable Gold; sell maximum uses currency balance.

title: Ascension and what carries over
summary: Reawakening retains selected research and nightmare investments while rebuilding the kingdom.

sections.title: Entering prestige
paragraphs: The nightmare display becomes visible when total nightmares exceed zero. Awaken writes autosave-prestige and opens the Prestige scene. Starting a new kingdom from there triggers Reawaken and calls DoAscension.

rows: Currency, income totals, resources, resource upgrades
Machines, workflows, pipes, inventories, Armory, Portal

sections.title: Retained research runs callbacks
paragraphs: Retained technologies go through AddTech again, so OnUnlock effects run for the new player. A Utility that adds workflows or machine capabilities can have those effects again. The retention filter checks the exact NodeType, not whether the name sounds like automation.

sections.title: Active nightmare display
paragraphs: NightmareCountActive is an ascension snapshot used to display newly gained nightmares as a +difference. Endgame multipliers use total NightmareCount, so newly earned nightmares can affect later runs before ascending.

title: Prestige perks and refunds
summary: All nine perks and their exact rank formulas.

sections.title: Ranks and refunds
paragraphs: A zero-point perk has zero effect. Rank n costs n nightmares: first rank 1, second 2, third 3. Total rank-n investment is n(n+1)/2. Unspent nightmares equal total NightmareCount minus all invested rank costs. Left click buys a rank when affordable; right click refunds a rank; Reset sets every perk to zero.

sections.title: Application
paragraphs: Research discount multiplies generated research currency collections. Resource discount is read by player resource upgrades, Forest crew upgrades, and Farm upgrades. Human quality is added during human resource generation; equipment and dark-essence quality are added in the relevant crafting-result creation. Human health is included in HumanItemData health calculation; sell value is read by Shop and LuxuryShop. Manual productivity is read by RecipeElement. Manual crafting adds the perk value to current Productivity before accumulating productivity progress; equipment manually receives a further ×0.5 factor.
The purchase handler has no explicit per-perk rank cap. The formulas above are literal source behavior; extrapolated extreme ranks are not balanced-design recommendations.

title: Nightmares and the endgame loop
summary: Distilled nightmares, fragments, distiller charging, and enemy scaling.

sections.title: Earning nightmares
paragraphs: The endgame dungeon final boss lists FragmentedNightmareReward and DistilledNightmareReward. Distilled reward is ready when NightmareActive and NightmareProgress>0.99, or unconditionally when total nightmares are zero. Receiving it increases the total, updates the Steam stat, subtracts 1 charge if charge≥1, partially resets North war, and opens the victory popup for the first nightmare.

Fragmented reward creates fragmented_nightmare with chance 1 and amount 2. It is enabled while nightmare mode is active, or while the total is zero. The quest overloads for both rewards are empty; their dungeon overloads perform the reward.

sections.title: The distiller
paragraphs: nightmare_distiller follows dungeon_endgame and additionally checks that the last endgame CompletedCount entry is positive. The machine class is NightmareCollector, displayed as nightmare_distiller. Its one-item input consumes nightmare_collector items.

Below full charge, each consumed item adds 1/floor(sqrt(totalNightmares)). Values between 0.985 and 1 are snapped to 1. At 1–3 nightmares each item fills a charge, at 4–8 it fills half, and at 9–15 it fills one-third. The machine Update itself does not check NightmareActive; reward eligibility and enemy multipliers do.

sections.title: Toggle and repeat access
paragraphs: The distiller UI toggles NightmareActive. Difficulty readers require IsEndgame and NightmareActive. A distilled reward changes North war from stage index 4 back to 3; when at index 3, progress is set to 10. This partial reset requires the final war section to be secured again, independently of ascension.

title: Saves, autosaves, pause, and offline behavior
summary: Storage, recovery behavior, persisted state, timing, and offline progression evidence.

sections.title: Storage and format
paragraphs: Files are stored in Application.persistentDataPath + /Saves. New saves use .save and gzip-compressed UTF-8 JSON. Recall tries gzip then plain JSON after IOException. The browser accepts .json and .save. Each save stores Application.version, Player, and a hash-derived Secret; the inspected LoadState does not validate Secret.

Store uses FileMode.Create, so saving over a name replaces it. Saving rejects a player with zero workflows. Errors show a persistent status and log the exception. File modification time is filesystem metadata, not a simulated elapsed-time field.

sections.title: Autosaves
paragraphs: Default frequency is 300 simulated seconds (5 minutes). Three rotating files are autosave-0 through autosave-2. Missing slots are filled first; otherwise the oldest file by last-write time is replaced. Option 0 disables timed autosaves.
Extra checkpoints are autosave-exit on quitting, autosave-rtt on return to menu, and autosave-prestige before prestige. Continue selects the latest file across all recognized saves.

sections.title: Persisted player state
paragraphs: Player JSON includes workflows and contents, balances and earned totals, exchange data, research, resources and upgrade counts, camera/zoom/current workflow, upgrade counts and availability, requisition types, wars, unlocked dungeons, game time, Forest/Farm settings, quest/dungeon metadata, Armory, Portal, Register, ascension/nightmare state, and perks. Options and bindings are in separate PlayerPrefs.

sections.title: Loading older saves
paragraphs: LoadState restores the prior in-memory player if loading throws. Before version 0.9.6, patches grant training_grounds_spec when Training Grounds is unlocked and set NightmareProgress=1 and NightmareActive=true. This does not establish compatibility with arbitrary future/edited formats.

sections.title: Pause and offline behavior
paragraphs: WorldFlowManager advances the player with Time.deltaTime. Autosave timers also use Time.deltaTime. In-game menu sets timescale=0 and disables controls; closing restores timescale=1. Steam overlay pauses similarly and restores only when the in-game menu is closed.

No wall-clock catch-up calculation was found in the inspected load path. Filesystem time orders saves; it is not fed into workflow/resource simulation. This build therefore has no verified offline progression in the examined code. Loading reconstructs saved state and resumes delta-time simulation.

title: Controls and rebinding
summary: Factory keyboard and mouse bindings decoded from the actual action-map asset.

sections.title: Factory bindings
paragraphs: PlayerPrefs overrides can replace these defaults. Generated InputActions stores its JSON on one physical source line, cited for this complete table.

sections.title: Combinations
paragraphs: Alt+V is the ToggleUI composite; V alone is AreaMove. Shift plus mouse wheel cycles workflows while the world is visible and more than one workflow exists. Ordinary wheel changes camera zoom when UI does not block it. Ctrl bypasses blueprint grid snapping. Shift keeps a blueprint ready after placement.
Mouse traversal binds middle, right, and left buttons. Left-button traversal rejects most UI interactions and busy drag/drop. Right click also cancels, so behavior depends on context.

sections.title: Rebinding
paragraphs: Rebindable actions are Purchase, Tech, Deco, Resources, Picker, Deconstruct, Clone, AreaMove, Search, Map, ItemMenu, and hotkeys 1–0. Escape, traversal, ordinary mouse interaction, and Alt+V are not in that exposed rebind list. Apply writes InputBindingOverrides JSON in PlayerPrefs; Reset removes overrides; closing without Apply restores the captured original settings.

sections.title: Technology gates
paragraphs: Clone requires clone_tool, area move requires unlock_area_move, and ItemMenu requires item_list. Numeric keys call GameUI.DoHotkey and operate contextually in the current interface; a shortcut does not bypass research gates.

title: Building, copying, and area movement
summary: Placement ghosts, costs, snapping, repeated builds, cloned networks, and moving groups.

sections.title: Placement
paragraphs: Click a purchase row for a blueprint or drag it for drag placement. Ghost footprints turn red on flow-collider overlap. Ctrl bypasses grid snapping. Placement checks affordability, spends cost, creates a copy, and positions it. Individual overlap shows NoSpace.

sections.title: Repeated builds and copied networks
paragraphs: Shift keeps the ghost active and updates cost for another placement. Otherwise blueprint mode ends and the buy menu may reopen. Cancel closes the ghost.

Copying a decorated container can include anchored machines/decorations. The game maps originals to copies, reconnects pipes whose two endpoints are copied, and offsets intermediate pipe nodes. That loop does not recreate connections to machines outside the selection.

sections.title: Area copy
paragraphs: clone_tool gates area copy. Overlapping colliders select machines first to establish a blueprint root, then decorations. A selection containing only decorations does not create an area-copy root in this implementation. The rectangle previews combined costs; very tiny selections are ignored.

sections.title: Area movement
paragraphs: unlock_area_move gates area movement. It creates an invisible temporary parent decoration and starts its drag mover to move existing parts instead of purchasing copies. Container movement uses anchored parts.

sections.title: Blueprint persistence
paragraphs: These classes implement in-memory placement/copy ghosts. No separate exported blueprint library or import/export format was found here. Normal player saves persist layouts and configuration.

sections.title: Additional workflows
paragraphs: add_diagrams research adds a workflow; element_stacking follows it. Extra workflows cost 100,000 raw-Gold-equivalent in Rings plus 100,000 in Gold while fewer than five workflows exist, otherwise Crowns replace Gold. The collection is multiplied by 1.3^(current workflow count).

title: Options, display, audio, language, and accessibility
summary: Exposed settings and how they are stored.

rows: Deduplicated modes at least 1280×720; unmatched current mode shown as Custom
Saved target; default rounds display refresh-rate ratio
On without explicit target or when target is within 5 FPS of refresh, otherwise off
Whole minutes; default 5; zero disables timed autosaves
PlayerPrefs Locale; resource and language.ini handling

sections.title: Scale limits
paragraphs: Maximum scale is 1.0 below 1080 pixels high, 1.25 below 1440, 1.75 below 2160, and 2.5 at 2160 or above. Scale changes refresh font filtering and main/game/prestige canvases. The slider can commit on mouse release, so Cancel does not necessarily undo an already applied live scale change.

sections.title: Language loading
paragraphs: Resources/Language TextAssets define locales. en-US is the fallback. A language.ini file in the process working directory overrides locale selection. Otherwise saved Locale is used; without one, the current culture is used only if exactly available, else en-US. Missing translations fall back to English, then show @key and log a warning.
Key=value text skips semicolon comments. A value beginning with @ aliases an already-read key. Applying locale changes current thread culture and UI culture.

sections.title: Accessibility evidence
paragraphs: OptionsUI provides scale, rebinding, resolution and independent volumes. It does not expose dedicated colorblind, screen-reader, subtitle, or reduced-motion switches. That describes this options class, not a platform-wide accessibility certification.

sections.title: Persistence
paragraphs: Unity PlayerPrefs store options separately from kingdom saves. Apply stores framerate/autosave settings and volume values, and updates global options. Different saves do not select separate options profiles.

title: Character names and random generation
summary: Stable seeded names, six cultures, surname patterns, and live versus deterministic rolls.

sections.title: Stable names
paragraphs: HumanDetailsPopup creates a random stream from the human item GetSeed() plus NameGen, then generates and displays FullName. The same seed with the same generator implementation produces the same name when reopened. This is derived presentation rather than a separate stored rename system.

sections.title: Assembly
paragraphs: Given names combine a weighted start, random syllable count, weighted middles and ending. Weighted surname patterns include compound, root/suffix, prefix, patronymic, place, two-part and fixed pool; cultures use their own subsets. Cleaning collapses selected repeated vowels/consonants and capitalizes space/hyphen-separated parts.
WeightedList sums max(1,weight), samples an integer below the total, and chooses the cumulative matching entry. Empty lists throw. Culture selection uses the same minimum-one weight rule.

sections.title: Seeds and distributions
paragraphs: SeedGenerator hashes ASCII string bytes through a 64-bit xor/multiply FNV-style hash with separator bytes. JSON object keys are sorted; array order is retained. SeededRandom advances and mixes a 64-bit state. Integer ranges are lower-inclusive, upper-exclusive; RandomFloat is in [0,1). RandomGaussian uses a Box–Muller-style transform; RandomScatter uses standard deviation baseVal×scatter/2. Item seeds contain eight alphanumeric characters.

sections.title: Reproducibility limits
paragraphs: Research prices use a fresh stream seeded by identifier. Human names use item seed plus NameGen. Live choices may use Global, seeded from DateTime.Now.Ticks for the process. The inspected player save does not serialize Global’s state; a stable item seed does not make every global future roll replayable.

title: Achievements, Steam statistics, and integration
summary: Every direct achievement trigger, statistic threshold, and source limitation.

sections.title: Direct triggers
paragraphs: These are actual Steam IDs, not invented display names. Criteria are verified at call sites. Recipe-family IDs can have multiple call sites; the table cites the first.

rows: Purchase all non-developer, non-hidden FlowElement nodes.
Purchase all non-developer, non-hidden Recipe nodes.
Purchase every non-developer, non-hidden technology considered by the current player check.
After AddEquipment, the equipped-item count reaches at least 10 (the EquipmentSlot enum count).
AddEnhancement leaves all three slots occupied: Engrave, Enchant, Blessing.
Process Gold income through GamePlayer.AddCurrency with isIncome=true; normally the first earned Gold.
A human reaches zero health in damage handling with indulgence in the Scroll slot.
Start the new kingdom from Prestige.
Complete any of these recipes: demonsteel_helm, demonsteel_armor, infected_shield, hellish_mask, hellish_cover, archmage_hat, archmage_robe.
Complete any of these recipes: vanquisher_sword, blighted_dagger, blink_rapier, flenser_greatsword, unblinking_axe, deadeye_bow, fragment_staff, unlife_staff.
WarEffort consumes a combatant and adds it to an active war.
Finish the direct widget recipe at Inventor; the callback is not attached to tinker.
Earned raw Gold / 10,000, so thresholds are 5m; 50m; 500m raw units = 500; 5,000; 50,000 displayed gold coins.

sections.title: Backend limits
paragraphs: SteamStat updates once per simulated second and stores immediately on threshold crossings. SteamStatsManager also stores every 300 seconds and at quit. The backend definition table mapping statistic tiers to achievement display names/IDs is absent from this source; those names are not fabricated.

Gold sends player earned total/10,000 through a monotonic Set. Quest and boss counters use Add and can accumulate in the Steam account separately from a kingdom save. Ascension resets player income history but does not lower an already higher Steam statistic through Set.

sections.title: Steam lifecycle
paragraphs: SteamManager initializes Steamworks and requests relaunch under application ID 4538080 when necessary, runs callbacks, and shuts down the API on destruction. SteamAchievement.Trigger de-duplicates IDs in a process-local HashSet before checking Initialized and calling GetAchievement, SetAchievement and StoreStats. An uninitialized trigger is not sent by that call.

Steam overlay pauses simulation. SaveGame handles local files without a Steam Cloud synchronization API in that path; client configuration may still synchronize files externally, so source alone cannot certify Cloud support.

summary: Shrine follows Scribe and requires Yensburg war stage 2. It grants prayer_1 and uses Faith for many recipes/upgrades. Catacombs requires Yensburg stage 3, North war Yensburg stage 4, Archive North stage 1, and endgame North stage 4. Distiller additionally checks endgame completion.
